description: Somos Geoteam, un equipo de 3 Ingenieros de Sistemas (Full-Stack, Cloud & IA) listos para construir un MVP geoespacial en tiempo real. Desarrollaremos una plataforma inteligente que conecta datos satelitales y climáticos de la NASA para ayudar a agricultores a anticipar sequías, heladas y desastres naturales, optimizando sus cultivos con IA predictiva.
summary:
We developed TerraQuipu, an agro-climatic decision-support ecosystem featuring an offline-first mobile PWA for Andean smallholder farmers and a GIS Web Studio with an integrated El Niño climate stress simulator. 

TerraQuipu directly addresses the challenge of soil conservation under extreme climate volatility by fusing real NASA satellite telemetry (POWER agroclimatology, SMAP L4 soil moisture, FIRMS thermal hotspots, GPM precipitation, and SRTM 30m DEM) with participatory in-situ soil fist tests ("allpa t'ikay"). In the Web Studio, agronomists simulate El Niño drought scenarios based on SENAMHI/ENFEN regional anomalies (-24% rainfall deficit, 42% root-zone moisture reduction).

This is critically important because the 2026–2027 El Niño severely threatens rainfed Andean agriculture. TerraQuipu converts coarse orbital data into parcel-level biological rotations with native legumes (Tarwi/Haba), fixing up to +95 kg N/ha, cutting chemical fertilizer costs, disrupting potato weevil pests by >75%, and enforcing strict zero-burning practices to preserve living topsoil.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

TerraQuipu is a dual-tier agro-climatic intelligence platform that bridges spaceborne Earth observations with indigenous Andean agriculture:

- Web Studio & Visor (Regional Simulation Tier): Built for agronomists and basin authorities. It ingests live elevation models (Copernicus 30m / NASA SRTM) and SMAP L4 volumetric soil moisture, computing real 2D finite-difference slope gradients. It features an El Niño Climate Stress-Testing engine that modulates baseline satellite telemetry using official SENAMHI/ENFEN historical anomalies (-24% rainfall to 510 mm, and a 0.58 moisture factor) to evaluate parcel vulnerability before planting.

- Mobile PWA (Tactical Mitigation Tier): Designed for Quechua smallholder farmers operating in disconnected mountain quebradas. It works 100% offline via an indexed local Outbox. Instead of burdening farmers with complex probabilistic graphs, it translates climate risk into immediate, actionable field rules: prohibiting crop residue burning (validated via NASA FIRMS), prescribing native legume rotations, and conducting participatory ground-truth soil tests ("allpa t'ikay").

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

-Biological Soil Regeneration: Rotating potato monocultures with native Andean legumes (*Tarwi / Lupinus mutabilis* and *Faba beans*) captures +75 to +95 kg of atmospheric nitrogen per hectare.

- Economic Insumo Savings: Eliminates the need for 3.3 bags of synthetic urea per hectare, saving farmers between S/ 143 and S/ 300 per hectare (calculated in real time using official MIDAGRI SISAP local market fertilizer prices).

- Pest & Weevil Disruption: Interrupts the pupal cycle of the Andean Potato Weevil (*Premnotrypes spp.*) by over 75%.

-Wildfire & Topsoil Protection: Enforces a zero-burning rule supported by NASA FIRMS alerts, turning dry biomass into protective mulch to prevent convective storm erosion.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

- Frontend & PWA: Next.js 14, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Web Audio API (tactile auditory feedback).

- GIS Cartography: Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, PostGIS spatial geometries.

- Backend & Ingestion APIs: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NASA POWER REST API, Open-Meteo elevation & soil APIs.

- Database & Cloud Automation: Supabase (PostgreSQL 15 + PostGIS), automated GitHub Actions cron jobs syncing NASA telemetry every 4 hours.

4. Creativity and Cultural Relevance

TerraQuipu connects the ancient computational wisdom of the Incan *Quipus* (used for astronomical planting cycles and granary accounting) and the concentric microclimatic terraces of Moray with 21st-century NASA satellite constellations.

5. Factors Considered

- Spatial Resolution Mismatch: Coarse satellite pixels (SMAP ~9–36 km, GPM ~10 km) cannot capture steep Andean ravines alone; we calibrate them using 30m SRTM DEM slopes and farmers' in-situ fist tests.

- Temporal Compression for El Niño 2026–2027: Because El Niño is already active, heavy earthworks (terraces, deep infiltration trenches) are deferred to the 2027 dry season, prioritizing immediate biological cover and rustic drought-tolerant crops.
